subject: Traffic-shaping validation & acceptance checklist for performance RFI
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmedata.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@acmedata.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance validation: requirements and acceptance criteria

Diego,

Thanks for taking this RFP item. Our procurement and SRE teams have a few focused asks around traffic shaping and how you propose to validate burst recovery, cost per token under mixed workloads, and deterministic latency SLOs. Specifically: 

- We need an acceptance checklist for test runs we can independently reproduce (scripts/profiles).
- A clear pass/fail derivation for tail latency (p95/p99/p999) with synthetic and reproducer traffic.
- How you model cache warming and prefix reuse across concurrency.
- Cost projection methodology (tokens, GPU hours, queuing overhead).

Can you provide a compact validation plan plus any existing scripts/profiles and an expected timeline to deliver benchmark artifacts? If possible, include a minimal set of measurements we can ask our infra team to reproduce within two weeks.

Regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Director, Procurement
Acme Data

--
Attachment: sample-rfi-questions.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.example.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmedata.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.example.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance validation: requirements and acceptance criteria

Hi Sarah — thanks, this is clear and actionable. High-level response below; I've attached a concise bench plan and two synthetic profiles you can use.

Summary of approach (short):
1) Test families: steady-state (fixed QPS), ramp & burst (spikes with varying concurrency), mixed-workload (short chat-like + long generation).
2) Metrics we will produce: throughput (tokens/sec), queuing latency, service latency (token wall time), p95/p99/p999, cold-start contribution, cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and estimated $/1M tokens.
3) Acceptance derivation: pass if p99 <= 200ms and p999 <= 600ms under your declared production mix for at least 95% of windows in a 30m run; cost delta within agreed guardrails. (We can tune thresholds per your SLA.)
4) Reproducibility artifacts: bench-plan (attached), synthetic_traffic_profiles.csv (attached), and a short runner script (we'll share a container image/runner link).

Notes on cache/prefix behavior:
- Prefix reuse: we recommend including a 20% prefix-reuse scenario in mixed profiles; our measurements include KV cache hit ratio and token-level latency breakdowns so you can quantify warming benefits.
- Burst recovery: we will run back-to-back spikes with progressively shorter cool-down windows to measure recovery slope and tail amplification. We report both transient (within-spike) and steady-state post-spike metrics.

Open questions for you so we can finalize acceptance criteria:
- Which model family/size do you expect to validate first (open-source 30B / 70B / custom weights)?
- Any hard constraints on acceptable p999 (absolute ms) or cost-per-1M tokens we should use for pass/fail?
- Can your infra team run an ephemeral GPU pool (approx 4x the expected production concurrency) to reproduce spikes, or should we run tests on our dedicated infra and provide artifacts?

I've CC'd Marissa for the formal checklist and Karthik for notes on quantization/throughput tradeoffs. We aim to hand over runnable artifacts within 4 business days once we get the model/constraints.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_bench-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf), synthetic_traffic_profiles.csv (text/csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmedata.com>, diego.fernandez@redwood.example.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance validation: requirements and acceptance criteria

Hi Sarah — adding the acceptance checklist as inline bullets so procurement/SRE have a single quick reference. I'll also attach an editable XLSX with explicit pass/fail logic and measurement windows.

Acceptance checklist (candidate):
- Test harness reproducibility: runner completes with exit code 0 and attaches raw logs and summary CSV.
- Measurement windows: 30m steady-state window; bursts are 2m spike windows with >50% traffic uplift.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 220ms, p999 <= 700ms for open-source 30B under the declared mix (if Acme requires tighter, list desired numbers).
- Recovery criteria: median recovery time to baseline throughput <= 90s after each burst.
- Cache warming evidence: show pre-warm vs cold-start run with per-prefix hit ratios and token-latency deltas.
- Cost estimate deliverable: $/1M tokens with breakdown (GPU-hours, queued tokens, and effective utilization).
- Artifact checklist: raw logs, aggregated CSV, flamegraphs of kernel time (optional), runner image tag, config file (YAML).

Notes: Karthik, can you add a short note about quantization/throughput expectations for customers validating on Ampere/Instinct hardware?

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acceptance_checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.example.com, marissa.cole@redwood.example.com, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmedata.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance validation: requirements and acceptance criteria

Sarah, quick tech addendum on hardware/quantization constraints: 

- For Ampere (A100/A30) families: expect 5-8% latency improvement when moving from FP16 to optimized 4-bit quantization for typical chat workloads, with a 2-4% drop in answer quality depending on model. We'll include eval prompts so you can sanity-check output drift.
- On AMD Instinct, throughput per GPU is roughly comparable at higher sequence lengths, but kernel availability for certain fused-attention optimizations may vary; our bench-plan flags fallback-kernel paths.
- When measuring cost per 1M tokens we account for: compute (GPU time * hourly gpu rate), storage IO for KV cache misses, and queueing inefficiency (measured as percent of tokens delayed beyond baseline latency). We provide a reproducible calculator (CSV + formula sheet) in the bench-plan.

I'll be available during your test window if you'd like live support.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Applied ML — Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
